questions: A VWP carries the same multicast source and group on VLAN 50 and VLAN 60. What prevents the sessions from aliasing?
Use one shared multicast session and add both VLANs as egress interfaces
A shared session loses the ingress VLAN context and cannot isolate policy state.
Change the multicast group address on the second VLAN
That changes the application group rather than fixing session identity.
Include ingress interface and VLAN ID in the multicast session key
The enhanced key separates otherwise identical multicast tuples by ingress context.
Disable multicast offload on every VWP member
Offload changes visibility and performance, not the session-key design.
Two mcast-session rows show the same source/group but different indev and vlanid values. What does this establish?
It proves every receiver has joined the multicast group
Receiver membership needs IGMP or application-side evidence.
It shows FortiOS is maintaining distinct VLAN-scoped sessions
Different session IDs and VLAN/interface fields demonstrate separate session identity.
It proves the upstream switch is forwarding all multicast frames
The FortiGate table cannot prove forwarding beyond its own interfaces.
It confirms the multicast policy is accepting every packet
Session presence alone does not establish policy outcome or packet delivery.
VLAN 60 multicast is missing while VLAN 50 works. Which check should come first?
Replace the multicast group with a new address
Changing the group hides the VLAN-specific cause instead of isolating it.
Disable all VLAN filtering on the switch fabric
That broadens the Layer 2 domain and can create a larger fault.
Enable PIM on every VWP interface
A transparent VWP session issue does not automatically require multicast routing.
Verify VWP wildcard-VLAN state, allowed VLANs and multicast policy interfaces
The VLAN tag must be admitted and match the intended policy path.
A CPU-side capture is empty but the multicast session shows NPU offload. What is the best interpretation?
The capture alone does not prove a drop; correlate NPU/session counters and a correct-interface capture
Offloaded traffic may not appear as expected in a CPU-side capture.
The session table must be stale and can be ignored
The session fields are useful evidence even when packet capture is limited.
The multicast receiver must be offline
Receiver state cannot be inferred from one local capture.
The VLAN tag is being stripped by the VWP
A missing capture does not identify VLAN-tag handling as the cause.
Chrony responds to FortiManager but NTP authentication fails. What should be compared first?
DNS search suffix and the FortiManager hostname
Name resolution is not the primary issue if the selected server is reachable.
The management interface MTU and TCP MSS
NTP uses UDP and this does not validate the authentication key.
Key ID, SHA-256 algorithm, key encoding and exact shared key
The authenticated NTP contract requires all four values to match.
The ADOM database version and policy package checksum
Those are unrelated to the NTP client authentication exchange.
What does diagnose system ntp status provide?
Proof that all FortiGate devices have synchronized to FortiManager
It reports FortiManager's NTP server state, not downstream device time.
NTP server information used to assess synchronization
It is the documented FortiManager verification command for NTP status.
A packet-level trace of every UDP/123 request and response
A status display is not a packet capture.
A report of all Chrony key-file entries on the Linux server
The server key file must be checked on the Chrony host.
Why can the same visible key string fail when one side uses HEX and the other ASCII?
The key bytes differ because the formats decode the string differently
The encoding is part of the authentication contract, not a cosmetic label.
SHA-256 automatically changes its digest length for ASCII keys
SHA-256 output length is fixed; the key input is what differs.
NTP key IDs are derived from the DNS name
The key ID is configured and must match on both systems.
Chrony accepts only hexadecimal keys for all NTP versions
Fortinet documents both hexadecimal and ASCII key examples.
Why protect FortiManager's time source with authentication?
It encrypts all FortiManager management sessions
NTP authentication does not replace HTTPS or SSH protection.
It synchronizes every FortiGate policy package automatically
Time sync does not install or synchronize configuration.
It makes the NTP server authoritative for all network devices
The setting configures FortiManager's own NTP client.
It protects event ordering, scheduled operations and time-sensitive checks
Accurate, trusted time improves correlation and operational correctness.
Two FortiAnalyzer data centers are connected only by routed WAN. Which HA mode fits the documented geo design?
Active-passive with a shared Layer-2 VIP stretched across sites
The documented routed geo design does not require a Layer-2 VIP.
Active-active with unicast heartbeat and no cross-site VIP
The active-active geo design supports Layer-3 peer connectivity.
Standalone nodes with manual daily log copy
Manual copying is not the documented HA architecture.
Active-passive with multicast heartbeat over the WAN
The documented design uses unicast heartbeat for geo HA.
Both FortiAnalyzer nodes have Initial Sync enabled during first cluster formation and the cluster stalls. What is the documented correction?
Disable Initial Sync on at least one node during initial formation
The primary is elected from nodes with Initial Sync disabled.
Enable a cluster VIP on both nodes before forming the group
A VIP is optional and requires Layer-2 connectivity.
Change the group name on the secondary to force election
The group identity must match across cluster members.
Disable log forwarding until the cluster becomes active
That does not resolve the initial synchronization election condition.
Which network protocol must be permitted between routed FortiAnalyzer geo-HA members?
UDP/123 for NTP
NTP may be required operationally but it is not the documented VRRP requirement.
TCP/443 for the GUI
GUI access does not carry the VRRP heartbeat.
IP protocol 112 for VRRP
Fortinet specifies that VRRP must pass between the members.
UDP/514 for syslog
Syslog transport is separate from the HA peer requirement.
What should a FortiGate use when both geo-HA FortiAnalyzer members are reachable?
Only the secondary address with fallback disabled
That prevents the documented primary/alternate recovery behavior.
A VIP that spans both data centers even without Layer 2
The guide says a VIP requires Layer-2 connectivity.
A single random peer chosen by DNS round robin
This is not the documented FortiGate alternate-server configuration.
Primary and alternate FortiAnalyzer addresses with fallback enabled
This gives the FortiGate an explicit alternate and return-to-primary behavior.
Which FortiSwitchOS models are documented for DCBX, ETS and PFC in 8.0.0?
FS-T1024E, FS-T1024F-FPOE, FS-2048F, FS-3032E and FS-3032G
These are the five models listed in the 8.0.0 release notes.
Every FortiSwitch model with a 10-Gigabit uplink
The feature has an explicit model list and is not universal.
Only the 100-series desktop switches
The release notes list high-density data-center models.
Any switch that supports LLDP-MED
LLDP support alone does not imply DCBX/ETS/PFC support.
Which LLDP DCBX TLVs are involved in the FortiSwitch 8.0 feature?
VLAN Name, Port Description, and Management Address only
Those are LLDP information elements, not the four DCBX TLVs.
ETS configuration, ETS recommendation, PFC configuration and application priority
These four TLVs exchange the relevant lossless-Ethernet behavior.
STP root, LACP system ID, and MACsec cipher suite
Those belong to other control-plane features.
DHCP relay, ARP inspection, and IGMP snooping
Those do not negotiate DCBX priority behavior.
What is a key ETS configuration constraint?
Every queue must have strict priority and unlimited bandwidth
ETS supports weighted groups as well as strict-priority groups.
PFC must be enabled on every priority group
A design needs both PFC-enabled and non-PFC/lossy classes.
The configured ETS priority-group rates must total 100 percent
The scheduler allocates guaranteed bandwidth across the groups.
The same CoS queue must belong to several priority groups
Each queue is assigned to a single priority group.
What trust model is required on a DCBX interface?
Trust IP DSCP and Dot1p simultaneously for the same interface
Fortinet says the DCBX interface does not trust both at once.
Trust only the physical port speed and ignore CoS
DCBX relies on priority classification, not just link speed.
Use a static route map to classify RoCE packets
Routing policy does not replace Layer 2 CoS mapping.
Use the 802.1p map profile and align both DCBX peers
Fortinet documents Dot1p trust and DCBX on both ends.
Where does the dynamic captive-portal URL come from?
The Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL vendor attribute in RADIUS Access-Accept
The controller reads attribute 27 from the authorization response.
A DHCP option returned before the client associates
The documented mechanism is a RADIUS Access-Accept attribute.
A CoA Disconnect-Request sent after portal authentication
CoA is a separate session-control transaction.
A static URL stored in the AP's radio profile
The feature is intended to use a per-session returned URL.
Which VAP configuration is required by the documented dynamic redirect feature?
Bridge mode with portal-type set to captive-portal-mac
Fortinet documents a tunnel-mode captive portal VAP.
Tunnel mode with portal-type set to auth-mac and dynamic redirect enabled
Those are the required VAP conditions in the configuration guide.
Tunnel mode with portal disabled and a static URL
The captive portal must be enabled for this flow.
Mesh mode with WPA3-Enterprise and RADIUS CoA
Mesh and WPA mode do not define this redirect feature.
The browser always receives the same portal URL. What evidence is most useful?
A channel utilization chart from the serving AP
RF utilization does not explain the authorization response URL.
The Access-Accept contents for two users and the VAP dynamic-redirect setting
This compares the policy-supplied URL with the controller feature state.
The DHCP lease duration and default gateway metric
Those do not contain the RADIUS portal URL.
The FortiAP firmware image checksum only
Firmware integrity does not show whether attribute 27 was returned.
Why is the returned URL not equivalent to a CoA message?
Both messages are identical RADIUS attributes with different names
Access-Accept and CoA have different transaction roles.
CoA carries the portal HTML while Access-Accept carries credentials
The documented dynamic URL is in Access-Accept attribute 27.
The URL is selected by DHCP after the client authenticates
The policy engine returns it in the RADIUS authorization response.
Access-Accept supplies the redirect target; CoA changes an existing authorization state
The messages serve different points in the session lifecycle.
FortiNAC RADIUS logs show anonymous and LDAP policy matching fails. What should be checked first?
Rebuild the switch topology and change the authentication VLAN
The visible username and directory mapping should be inspected first.
Disable LDAP synchronization across every directory
That removes identity data instead of correcting its representation.
The exact identity received, endpoint identity privacy and LDAP domain format
A username/domain mismatch can prevent directory user resolution.
Move the catch-all policy to the top of the list
A catch-all can hide the identity failure and broaden access.
How does FortiNAC treat a configured LDAP domain name?
It requires an exact domain match when the login supplies a domain
The guide states that domain names must match exactly.
It accepts any child domain automatically
A configured example.com does not match it.example.com.
It strips all domain suffixes before every lookup
The parsing rules preserve and evaluate domain components.
It falls back to every directory after a mismatch
A configured mismatching domain causes immediate authentication failure.
What is the risk when multiple LDAP directories have no domain configured?
FortiNAC always queries them in administrator-defined order
The guide says the processing order cannot be controlled.
The first directory that authenticates the user is used
Different role or access attributes across directories can change results.
The user is forced to authenticate locally
Multiple directories are still used for authentication.
Duplicate user IDs are automatically merged into one identity
Unique identifier mappings are needed to avoid collisions.
What does RADIUS/LDAP authentication mean in FortiNAC?
LDAP validates the password while RADIUS only registers the host
The documented order is RADIUS validation and LDAP user data.
RADIUS and LDAP must return identical group lists before any record is created
The feature separates credential validation from user registration data.
LDAP replaces the RADIUS server for every authentication
RADIUS remains the credential validation source.
RADIUS validates credentials while LDAP supplies user registration data
The guide notes a local user record may still be created if LDAP lacks the user.
A client certificate has a CDP but no OCSP URI. Why can Local RADIUS reject it?
Local RADIUS uses OCSP and does not use the CDP/CRL path
The documented Local RADIUS revocation method is OCSP from certificate AIA.
The certificate must include two CDP URLs for redundancy
The limitation is the absence of an OCSP responder URL.
The client must use PEAP without TLS
The issue is revocation-source support, not the EAP method choice.
FortiNAC-F cannot validate any corporate CA
It can validate client certificates against trusted root certificates.
Where must the endpoint CA chain be installed for Local RADIUS EAP-TLS?
Server Certificates under the Local RADIUS Server target
Server certificates are not automatically added to endpoint trust.
General Trusted CA only
The specific Local RADIUS trust target is required.
RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] under Trusted Certificates
That target is used to validate Local RADIUS EAP-TLS client certificates.
SAML Trust (Admin) for administrator logins
That target is for administrative SAML identity, not EAP-TLS endpoints.
Why must OCSP reachability be tested on both FortiNAC-F HA nodes?
Both nodes query OCSP for every request simultaneously
The control node performs the query, including after failover.
The in-control node may change after failover and must reach the responder
DNS/HTTP reachability and trust chain must exist on the takeover node.
The secondary node stores the CRL instead of the primary
Local RADIUS does not use CRL imports as its revocation method.
OCSP uses VRRP and therefore needs a Layer-2 cluster
OCSP is an HTTP-based status query to the responder URL.
CRL checking is mandatory in the PKI design. What is the supported alternative?
Disable certificate validation on Local RADIUS
That removes the revocation control rather than meeting the requirement.
Import the CRL into the Local RADIUS trust target
The Local RADIUS flow has no documented CRL import option.
Add the CDP URL to the FortiNAC-F Local Service page
The Local RADIUS service does not expose a CDP field.
Terminate EAP-TLS on a CRL-capable external RADIUS server and proxy from FortiNAC-F
This moves revocation checking to a RADIUS service that supports CRL validation.
What is the main benefit of TACACS+ client groups in FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2?
They replace all individual TACACS+ client definitions
The clients still exist as individual network-device objects.
They automatically create a new identity realm for each subnet
Client grouping is a policy-target abstraction.
They let one policy target a reusable set of network-device clients
This avoids selecting hundreds of devices individually.
They convert TACACS+ requests into RADIUS requests
The feature does not change the protocol.
How can a TACACS+ policy target devices after client groups are created?
Select individual clients, client groups, or both in the policy
FortiAuthenticator supports a combination of those policy targets.
Select only the end-user LDAP group
The group here contains TACACS+ clients, not users.
Bind the group to a FortiGate firewall policy
TACACS+ client groups are consumed by FortiAuthenticator policies.
Add the group name to the TACACS+ shared secret
Membership is configured as an object relationship.
Which username formats are documented for TACACS+ policy identity?
Only user@domain.com
The policy supports multiple realm separators.
username@realm, realm\username, and realm/username
These are the documented input formats.
Only NetBIOS\host\user
That is not the complete supported list.
IP-address/username and MAC-address/username
Those are device identifiers, not the policy username formats.
Which API resource manages TACACS+ client-to-group associations?
/radiusclientgroups/
That endpoint is not the documented TACACS+ association resource.
/tacpluspolicy/
The policy object is separate from group membership.
/tacplusrealms/
Realm configuration is not client-group membership.
/tacplusgroupclient/
FortiAuthenticator documents this endpoint for client/group associations.
What is an Instruction Profile in FortiPAM 1.9?
A replacement credential stored inside the secret
Credentials remain in the secret object.
A policy that grants guests permission to check out all secrets
Access authorization is separate from instruction content.
A reusable formatted guidance object that can be attached to secrets
The profile is independent of the secret and can be reused.
A session-recording format that stores terminal video
Recording is a separate FortiPAM function.
When is Instruction Resources Allocation (%) required to be greater than zero?
When uploading or inserting instruction-profile images and videos
Media resources require allocated storage.
For every text-only instruction profile
The requirement is specifically for resource uploads/media.
Only when rotating a secret password
Password rotation is unrelated to instruction media.
Only when enabling TACACS+ authentication
TACACS+ is a separate product workflow.
How does a secret display its Guest Instruction profile?
The profile is inferred from the secret's folder name
The secret has an explicit Guest Instruction field.
Attach the profile in the secret's Settings tab
The secret references the reusable profile through that field.
Add the profile as a new credential field
The instructions are not part of the credential material.
Set the guest's LDAP group to the profile name
The profile is attached to the secret, not the directory group.
What does attaching an instruction profile not do?
Render the formatted guidance during guest checkout
Rendering the guidance is the intended behavior.
Allow the same profile to be reused by several secrets
Reuse is explicitly supported.
Display referenced media in the instruction content
Media can be inserted when resources are allocated.
Grant the guest permission to access the secret
The guest must still be authorized to visit/check out the secret.
A FortiSIEM rule event has a username but no IP. Which action can populate an IP watchlist?
Resolve the username by querying DNS PTR records only
DNS reverse lookup does not provide the documented identity mapping.
Copy the IP from the last event for that username
That can target a stale address after DHCP or VPN changes.
Use LookupIpByUser in the Watch List Edit action
The function resolves the current mapping from Identity and Location.
Create a static watchlist entry from the username string
An IP watchlist needs a resolved address.
What data source does LookupIpByUser use?
The Identity and Location database's username-to-IP mapping
That is the documented lookup source.
The FortiGate routing table on the collector
Routing tables do not map a user identity to a current endpoint IP.
The SIEM's DNS cache only
The feature is based on Identity and Location data.
The Windows user profile's last logon timestamp
A timestamp alone does not resolve a network address.
The user moves from IP A to IP B. What should the dynamic watchlist do?
Keep IP A until an administrator deletes it manually
The feature is designed to update when the offending user changes IP.
Update the watchlist to the user's new IP
The documented behavior follows the current user-to-IP mapping.
Add every IP in the user's subnet
The lookup resolves the mapped address, not an entire subnet.
Disable the rule because DHCP changed the endpoint
Address changes are an intended dynamic-watchlist use case.
Another user is assigned the old IP. What should happen to that IP in the watchlist?
The IP should remain because it was once associated with the offender
That would risk blocking a different user.
The IP should be converted to a hostname entry
The watchlist is IP-based.
The IP should be duplicated under both users
The documented behavior removes the reassigned address.
The IP should be removed from the offender's watchlist
FortiSIEM accounts for another user taking that address.
What does a FortiSASE source IP anchor control?
The dedicated public IP used for SNAT based on user/group or country criteria
The anchor selects a deterministic egress address at the PoP.
The private IP assigned to the endpoint's Wi-Fi adapter
That is local endpoint addressing, not PoP egress NAT.
The city shown in an IP geolocation database only
Geolocation metadata is distinct from source NAT selection.
The identity provider used to authenticate the remote user
Authentication is a separate prerequisite and policy input.
Which source criterion granularity is documented for remote-user anchoring?
City-level user matching only
The guide distinguishes city-level IP geolocation from source matching.
Individual device MAC address at the PoP
The documented source criteria are user/group or country.
Country-level association or user/group selection
Country is the location criterion; user groups provide finer identity selection.
Autonomous system number and BGP community
Those are routing attributes, not the anchoring criteria.
How is source IP anchoring initially deployed?
By adding a public IP in the local FortiClient profile
The feature is provisioned on the FortiSASE backend.
Through a FortiCare request with license and PoP/user mapping details
The deployment guide requires backend implementation and sufficient IP licensing.
By creating a normal firewall VIP on the branch FortiGate
The anchor is applied at the FortiSASE security PoP.
By changing the endpoint's default route to a public address
The endpoint still tunnels to the PoP; the PoP applies SNAT.
A destination sees the wrong egress IP for one user group. What is the strongest verification?
Check the endpoint Wi-Fi RSSI and roaming history
Wireless RF does not prove PoP NAT selection.
Check only the public IP geolocation website
Geolocation metadata may lag and does not prove policy match.
Check whether the user can resolve the SaaS hostname
DNS resolution does not prove the selected SNAT address.
Compare the user's group/country criteria, PoP anchor and observed egress IP
This follows the policy selection through the actual data path.
A banking application requires a stable egress member for each client/destination pair. Which hash is best?
Round-robin across every eligible WAN
Round-robin changes member selection sequentially.
Measured-volume-based distribution
Volume balancing can reweight paths as traffic totals change.
Source-dest-ip-based
The same source/destination pair is kept on the same member.
Inbandwidth steering
That selects by available inbound bandwidth, not pair identity.
What is the distinction between source-ip-based and source-dest-ip-based?
One pins all destinations for a source; the other pins each source/destination pair
The hash key has different granularity.
One uses TCP ports and the other uses UDP ports
These modes are IP-based, not transport-port hashes.
One selects only SLA-failed links and the other selects healthy links
Eligibility is a separate strategy decision.
One is for IPv6 only and the other is for IPv4 only
Both can be used with the relevant SD-WAN service family.
What does weight-based load balancing primarily distribute by?
Total packet bytes per WAN
Measured-volume mode uses traffic volume.
The number of sessions on each member relative to configured weights
Weight-based mode uses session-count ratios.
The source country of each remote user
That is a FortiSASE anchoring criterion.
The latency of each Performance SLA probe only
SLA latency is an eligibility/quality input, not the weight count.
In an SLA load-balancing rule, what does the SLA strategy decide?
Which source IP address is used for SNAT
SNAT is handled by the firewall policy/NAT configuration.
Which RADIUS group authenticates the user
RADIUS identity is unrelated to SD-WAN member selection.
How many sessions are created per application
The strategy does not define session creation.
Which members are eligible based on the configured SLA
Hash mode then distributes flows among the selected members.
Which command pair best separates link eligibility from actual service selection?
diagnose sys sdwan health-check status and diagnose sys sdwan service4 <id>
The first shows probe/SLA state; the second shows service mode and selected members.
get system status and diagnose debug application httpsd
Those do not show SD-WAN probe and service selection.
diagnose firewall iprope list and execute ping
They do not expose the full SD-WAN service decision.
show system interface and get router info bgp summary
Those provide interface/routing context but not the service's selected members.
What does source-IP hashing not guarantee after a member failure?
That the same client will normally hash consistently while the member set is stable
That is the purpose of source-IP affinity.
That a new flow from the same source uses the same selected member in steady state
This is the documented source-IP behavior.
That the public egress IP remains identical after route/NAT/member changes
Hash affinity is not a persistent public-IP reservation.
That different sources can be distributed across different members
Different source addresses can hash to different members.
